provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: The original rule works like this. The input is a small tile of one colour on background 0. Let s be the number of background cells and n the number of coloured cells. The output is a background canvas of (3s)x(3s), viewed as an s x s grid of tile slots. n unchanged copies of the tile are stamped into those slots in reading order: k-th copy at slot (k//s, k%s). Under a D4 transform, the whole output is transformed, so each stamped copy becomes a copy of the visible (transformed) input tile. Only the slot fill order moves. The factory computes the image of slot (q, p) on the s x s slot grid for each of the 8 D4 elements. It emits that as a direct coordinate formula; for example, d4=1 fills columns top-to-bottom starting from the rightmost column. Colour roles use background = palette[0]. s and n are counted relative to that constant, and the visible input tile is copied verbatim. No normalization, inverse rotation or colour unpermutation is used.
draft_notes.limitations: Assumes the background is exactly palette[0], as in the constructor. It does not infer the background from demos. The constructor always produces square 3x3 tiles with 2..6 coloured cells, so s >= 3 and n <= s*s. The emitted code uses the visible h and w generally and guards n > s*s and s == 0, but those cases are outside the generator's domain. I found no constructor defects or fixture contradictions: all four train pairs and the test pair match the uniform rule. These programs have not been executed by me.
